blocks.text: Ependi is one of the best-loved characters of Turkmen humour. He is the hero of a great many short, funny stories: a man of modest means, often with his donkey, who seems foolish one moment and wiser than anyone the next.

He is not only Turkmen. The same character is known across a wide area, from the Arab world to Central Asia, as Nasreddin Hodja, Molla Nasreddin, Juha, Afandi and other names. Encyclopaedia Britannica calls him a legendary figure of folk literature, a wise fool; whether a real man stands behind the stories is unknown. Each people tells them in its own way, with its own details and names, and in Turkmen he is Ependi.

In 2022 UNESCO added the tradition of telling these anecdotes to its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, on a joint request from seven countries: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Türkiye, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. UNESCO describes stories built on wisdom, witty replies, absurdity and surprise, in which the hero gets out of a tight spot by the power of words. People of every age tell them, in conversation, in books and on children's television.
Here are two of the best-known stories, in our own words.

blocks.title: Eat, my coat
blocks.text: Ependi goes to a wedding feast in his everyday clothes. Nobody offers him a seat, and nobody brings him food. He slips home, puts on his finest coat and comes back. Now he is led to the place of honour and served first. Ependi dips his sleeve into the soup and says: “Eat, my coat, eat! It's you they invited, not me.”

blocks.title: The donkey isn't here
blocks.text: A neighbour knocks and asks to borrow Ependi's donkey. “Sorry,” says Ependi, “the donkey isn't here.” Just then the donkey brays loudly in the yard. “But I can hear it!” says the neighbour. Ependi looks hurt: “So you believe a donkey and not me?”

Like many of these tales, both are short enough to tell over a cup of tea, and both end with a line people quote in daily life. That is how the stories are used: to make a point, win an argument or laugh at someone who judges people by their clothes.
With the words of this unit, you can read this:

blocks.tk: Ependi akylly adam. Ol baý däl, ýöne bagtly. — Ependi, sen akyllymy? — Hawa, elbetde! Eşek hem akylly.
blocks.en: Ependi is a clever man. He isn't rich, but he is happy. — Ependi, are you clever? — Yes, of course! The donkey is clever too.

vocab.en: Ependi, the wise fool of Turkmen anecdotes

questions.q: Which countries asked UNESCO to list the telling of these anecdotes?
options: No country: they are a modern TV show
questions.explain: Seven countries asked together in 2022, Turkmenistan among them.

questions.q: Why does Ependi feed his coat?
options: Because the hosts honoured the coat, not the man

questions.q: In *Ol baý däl*, what does *däl* do?
options: It asks whether he is rich
questions.explain: *däl* after a word says **not**: *baý däl*, not rich.
